title: UX, information architecture and conversion
summary: Help people find information, understand choices and finish important tasks.
why: A website that hides answers wastes search and ad traffic.
Clear paths, forms and error handling reduce confusion and abandonment.
know: Organize navigation, pages, content and calls to action around user tasks rather than the company org chart.
Forms and shopping flows need loading, empty, error, success and recovery states.
Keyboard access, focus, labels, contrast and mobile use are basic requirements. Interpret conversion changes with traffic quality.
inputs: Priority audiences, main tasks, funnel data or support questions
Content inventory, device mix and brand rules
actions: Map task flows, sitemap and page order; state the concern each step resolves.
Build an interactive prototype covering main and failed paths.
Test keyboard use, forms, narrow screens and actions. Plan experiments when traffic is sufficient.
done: Main tasks work from entry to completion; errors are understandable and recoverable.
Events match the hypothesis; reported improvements include sample and period.
pitfalls: Equating more clicks with better business outcomes.
decision: Agree on the main user task and tradeoffs between brand, information and simplicity.

reader.concept: UX is the experience of completing a task. Information architecture organizes content; conversion design makes the next action clear.
reader.when: Use this when people cannot find information, finish forms or complete purchases.

example.situation: A product page has beautiful images but no visible shipping or return information.
example.lesson: Answer purchase questions before changing button colors.

reader.first_step: Walk through one main task from arrival to completion.
